description:
REVIEWED 2026-10-25 (TodoReview) against origin/develop 9a184b619 and fork main ea44bcc9 (30.24.0.13). PROBLEM
The SQLite unpadded-date defect (TPC-DS and OBT Q16/Q94/Q95 filtering on NULL date bounds, fixed in BenchBox #3426 / fork 30.24.0.13) passed `make sql-execution-gate` because at the gate scale (SF0.01) those queries produce no signal on the reference engine. Equality of two non-informative results proves nothing about translation.

VERIFIED FACTS (2026-10-25, executed)
- DuckDB on TPC-DS SF0.01 (1 warehouse row) returns exactly ONE row `(0, None, None)` for Q16, Q94 and Q95 for seeds default, 1001 and 7. They are NOT zero-row results, so any row-count or `rows non-empty` test treats them as signal. The original item text ('return no rows') was wrong on this point; the mechanism is an aggregate over an empty set.
- scripts/sql_execution_gate/gate.py `_evaluate_cell` checks error, row-count vs TPC expected count (`expected_row_counts`), `first_difference` vs DuckDB, and baseline difference. None of the four classifies a result as vacuous, so empty-vs-empty and `(0,NULL,NULL)`-vs-`(0,NULL,NULL)` pass.
- tests/integration/test_tpcds_obt_equivalence.py is DuckDB-only (`build_engines` loads TPC-DS and the OBT parquet into DuckDB; no SQLite/Postgres/DataFusion). It therefore cannot detect any SQLite translation defect regardless of data. Its own vacuity rule (`_evaluate`: `not base_parts or not all(base_parts)` -> 'unverifiable') only sees zero-row parts, so a one-row zero/NULL aggregate counts as `equal`. Its UNVERIFIABLE lists name only zero-row bases (9 ids at SF0.01: 4,10,23,24,31,41,58,65,85; 2 at SF1: 23,24); Q16/94/95 are not on them.
- Seeds cannot fix this: with one warehouse Q16/94/95 are vacuous for every parameter (#3426). SQLite already times out on TPC-DS Q13/Q48 at SF0.01 (optional entries in scripts/sql_execution_gate/expected_differences.json), so a larger scale is not viable in the PR gate.
- #3426 produced non-vacuous evidence by giving catalog_sales/web_sales (and the OBT warehouse_sk for those channels) a second warehouse via `(item_sk % 2) + 1` in both engines and picking the state from the data; values recorded there: Q16 default 1/14385.84/1883.68, Q16 seed 1001 2/6022.84/-3046.96, Q94 default 1/6302.90/-6312.36, Q94 1001 1/586.38/753.49, Q95 default 1/4994.20/-3508.34, Q95 1001 1/10190.84/1105.66.

DECISION GATES (stop and ask the owner)
G1 Definition of vacuous. Options: (a) zero rows only (today's rule); (b) zero rows OR every row consists only of NULL/0 aggregate cells, i.e. no row carries a non-NULL non-zero value (recommended); (c) also flag any result whose reference has a single distinct value per column. Recommended default: (b).
G2 How to obtain non-vacuous evidence at gate scale. Options: (a) gate-only data augmentation (second warehouse as in #3426) for the known set plus an explicit 'unproven' list for the rest (recommended); (b) different seeds (does not help, see facts); (c) larger scale (not viable for SQLite/PR time); (d) list as unproven only. Augmented data lives only in the gate scratch dir and never reaches a published run.
G3 Gate policy for vacuous queries. Options: report-only; fail-closed with a reasoned allowlist that has stale-entry detection like expected_differences.json (recommended; this changes required-PR-job behaviour, so it needs owner approval before it blocks PRs).
G4 Confirm that gate-only augmented data is not an oracle stand-in or relaxed guard (it only makes the existing comparison informative; the DuckDB reference and baseline checks are unchanged).

GUARDRAILS
- Never add expected_differences.json entries to hide vacuity; never loosen rel_tol/abs_tol in rows.py; never weaken existing checks.
- Do not change dsdgen/dbgen output for any published or CLI run; augmentation is gate-scratch only.
- Do not move queries between 'equal' and 'unverifiable' in the OBT lists without recording the executed reason; the lists must stay self-checking (test_expected_lists_are_well_formed).
- Keep PR gate wall time inside the existing job timeout; record before/after.
